message.content:
Review: The problem is clearly framed as a controlled, repeated-run comparison in the 111-unit array. It identifies the intervention (coupling), the main outcomes (spatial coarsening and subharmonic temporal order), and a plausible alternative explanation (a shared or direct response to the drive). The rationale appropriately distinguishes the target paper’s published claim from what the supplied aggregate data can establish, and it does not present correlation length as proof of causality.

Feedback: The measurement and analysis plan is unusually specific: it calls for synchronized signals, prespecified estimators and spectral criteria, run-level onset estimates, and treatment of non-crossing runs as censored. A few operational details remain open, including how coupling conditions and the drive-only comparison will be implemented, how the onset threshold and neighboring frequency bands will be calibrated, and how censoring and run-to-run variability will be handled statistically. “Drive-only” could also be defined more precisely in this system. These are design details to resolve, rather than major ambiguities in the research question.

Rating (1-5): 4
